title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment to quantify the operational effect of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipeline for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (shared initial candidate, ≤1 automated repair call per task), each task yielded a baseline (shared initial candidate) and a guarded final artifact (after validation and at most one repair). Primary estimand: absolute paired difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline), implemented as paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Results (N=200 pairs): baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded successes = 200/200 (1.000); contingency cells: n_11=199, n_10=1, n_01=0, n_00=0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI for absolute paired change = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered textual hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction in actionable errors) and the archived primary estimand were misaligned in wording versus scale assumptions: algebraic mapping shows the observed baseline actionable-error rate = 0.005 (1/200) and guarded = 0.0, yielding a 100% relative reduction but an absolute change of 0.005—far smaller than the preregistered absolute-effect calibration (0.15). We reconcile estimand notation, publish authoritative artifact digests for forensic recomputation, and discuss the power/design implications for rare-failure regimes.

sections.introduction: LLM-driven intent→configuration systems promise productivity gains for NetOps but raise safety concerns when generated commands are applied without deterministic checks. Operational proposals commonly interpose deterministic validators and bounded automated-repair adapters as guardrails in generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipelines. Yet quantitative, preregistered, artifact-hashed measurements of the marginal operational benefit from adding such validators under a constrained adapter contract are rare. We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Our principal contribution is a fully preregistered, artifact-hashed, paired confirmatory run with deterministic validator traces and complete provider-call accounting for forensic auditors.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification and runtime validators (e.g., header-space analysis, VeriFlow) provide pre-deployment safety primitives. Recent LLM→NetOps studies evaluate intent-driven generation (NetConfEval and others) but typically report single-condition accuracies or leaderboards without preregistration, per-episode deterministic validator traces, or adapter-accounting. Our work differs by (1) reusing the identical initial LLM candidate across baseline and guarded conditions (shared_initial generation), (2) applying a deterministic validator that produces canonical ASTs and simulator-backed semantic checks, (3) bounding repair budget (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1), and (4) archiving cryptographic digests for principal artifacts so auditors can reconstruct every reported contingency cell and per-episode trace.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and primary estimand. The study preregistration (cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001; SHA-256 above) froze design: N=200 paired intent→configuration tasks sampled from a deterministic synthetic multi-vendor generator (planned strata: Cisco-like N=66, Juniper-like N=67, RFC-neutral N=67), adapter contract enforcing shared_initial generation semantics, and maximum automated repair calls per task = 1. The registered primary_estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = not actionable-error). The preregistered confirmatory test is an exact McNemar two-sided test; we also prespecified a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The preregistration additionally recorded exclusion rules, retry rules, multiplicity plan, and sensitivity analyses (all archived with SHA-256 digests).
sections.results: Execution accounting and authoritative counts. Execution completed per the registered adapter: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation: 200; repair: 1) (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e2..., execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8..., analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...). The analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 consumed the raw results and produced the contingency table and inferential outputs. Primary paired outcome (artifact-grounded): complete_pair_count = 200; baseline_success_count = 199 (0.995); guarded_success_count = 200 (1.000); contingency cells (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051ba...): n_11=199, n_10=1, n_01=0, n_00=0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI for absolute paired difference = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA-256 = dbc0bd6b...).
sections.discussion: Estimand and hypothesis reconciliation. The preregistered textual hypothesis H1 asserted a ≥50% relative reduction in actionable-error rate. The archived primary_estimand and implemented analysis used an absolute paired success-rate difference. Algebraic mapping: actionable_error_rate = 1 − success_rate. Observed baseline actionable-error rate = 1 − 0.995 = 0.005 (1/200); guarded actionable-error rate = 0.0. The observed relative reduction = (0.005 − 0.0)/0.005 = 1.0 (100%), which meets the textual relative-reduction criterion. However, the preregistration's power calculation targeted detection of a large absolute reduction (absolute change ≈0.15), not a small absolute difference. Because the confirmatory test and power calibration operated effectively on different absolute scales, the registered decision rule (sized for large absolute effects) cannot be satisfied in a very-rare-failure regime even when the observed relative reduction is 100%. This mismatch explains the apparent contradiction between observing a guarded improvement and the preregistered confirmatory conclusion (H1 not supported under the original absolute-effect power sizing). Practical implication: relative reductions on near-zero baselines produce vanishing absolute differences; researchers should align effect-scale, estimand, and power assumptions when failures are rare.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment evaluating a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a bounded adapter contract. On the synthetic 200-task bank with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered large-absolute-effect hypothesis is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence (0.005) was far smaller than assumed in the preregistration's absolute-effect power calibration. We provide cryptographic hashes and precise artifact paths for all principal inputs, provider calls, validator traces, and analysis outputs so auditors can recompute contingency tables, per-vendor stratified counts, and the explicit discordant episode identifier from the archived evidence. Future studies should (1) expand model and validator diversity, (2) over-sample high-difficulty tasks when validating small absolute risk reductions, and (3) align estimand scale with practical cost-weighted failure metrics.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.

Per-vendor observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are not printed verbatim in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle text; auditors can compute them deterministically from the archived artifacts and provided SHA-256 digests.
